rounds.text: Decillion Finance Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of 1.21x on a book value of ₹ 32.9, which is slightly below the sector benchmark of 1.28x at 1.13x, offering an entry point below the industry standard [E1, E5]. The business demonstrates foundational long-term top-line expansion, achieving a compounded sales growth rate of 18% over a 10-year horizon [E9]. Recent operational adjustments are already yielding positive results, evidenced by year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% and accelerating earnings growth [E35, E36]. These green shoots signal an underlying operational turnaround that the market has yet to fully appreciate while the stock sits at just 20% of its 52-week range [E4]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a compounded sales decline of 63% alongside a negative return on equity of 0.5% [E8, E12].

Decillion Finance Ltd exhibits a severe and accelerating contraction in its top line, highlighted by a compounded sales growth rate of -63% over the trailing twelve months [E12]. This decay is structural rather than temporary, evidenced by worsening multi-year metrics including a 5-year sales contraction of -9% [E10] and a 3-year drop of -24% [E11]. Profitability metrics are essentially non-existent or negative, with both ROCE and ROE resting at -0.5% based on filed statements [E7, E8], while independent key-ratios place ROCE at an abysmal 0.09% against a sector benchmark of 5.52% [E6]. Compounding these operational failures, market expectations have completely detached from fundamental delivery as price growth recently exceeds profit growth by 135% [E26], leaving the stock lingering near the bottom at just 20% of its 52-week range [E4] alongside a total lack of shareholder return through a 0.00% dividend yield [E3].

Conceded: [E12], [E10], [E11], [E7], [E8], [E6], [E3]. Despite the multi-year top-line contraction cited by the bear, the company maintains a robust 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 18% [E9], demonstrating long-term structural viability that outweighs short-term volatility. The bear's critique of the stock sitting low in its 52-week range [E4] actually reveals an attractive valuation entry point backed by a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.13x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.28x [E5]. Furthermore, the bear's alarm over price growth exceeding profit growth [E26] ignores the active fundamental turnaround signaled by year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% [E35] and accelerating earnings growth [E36].

Conceded: [E9], [E35], [E36]. While the bull highlights a 10-year sales growth of 18% [E9], this figure is rendered obsolete by the catastrophic recent performance, where sales growth has plummeted to -24% over three years [E11], -9% over five years [E10], and a staggering -63% over the trailing twelve months [E12]. The bull’s reliance on [E35] and [E36] to suggest a turnaround is contradicted by the fact that the company is currently generating negative returns, with both ROCE and ROE sitting at -0.5% [E7], [E8]. Furthermore, the claim that the stock represents an attractive entry point [E4] ignores that the market is pricing in these fundamental failures, as evidenced by the fact that price growth is currently outpacing profit growth by 135% [E26]. The modest P/B ratio [E5] provides little comfort when the company fails to generate any dividend yield [E3] and exhibits an ROCE of only 0.09% compared to the sector benchmark of 5.52% [E6]. Ultimately, the bull’s focus on long-term averages ignores the reality that the company is currently in a state of severe, accelerating top-line decay [E12], [E30].
